title: Methods with explicit retrieval
caption: Complete comparison of methods with explicit retrieval: 20 retrieval-only and 90 document VQA methods. Ordering and date conventions follow Table 1 (representative explicit-retrieval methods); venue superscripts follow Table 4 (benchmark catalog). Mechanism specifies retrievers, evidence mappings, and retrieval training; Model gives the main generator model family. + denotes combinations and / alternatives; -- denotes unreported, unconfirmed, or inapplicable information.

conventions.ordering: Source row order is preserved. Within task groups, methods follow final conference submission deadlines, then first release within each conference; preprints/journal papers are inserted by first release (Table 1 convention).
conventions.dates: First release is separate from the citation year in the current BibTeX. YY.MM preferentially denotes the first arXiv version; an earlier official release, or the official release when no preprint exists, takes precedence. A -- month is unavailable and is stored as null, never as an invented month.
conventions.venue_superscripts: Venue superscripts F/W/D/S/I/C mean Findings, Workshop, Datasets and Benchmarks, Short, Industry, and competition reports, respectively.
conventions.superscripts: Plain JSON/CSV uses ^(x); Markdown displays x as a superscript.

notes: Header abbreviations. Deep = Deep Parsing; Gran. = Granularity; Acq. = Acquisition; Eval. = Evaluation.

Type labels. Deep and Learning list structure and training types directly; a standalone ✓ in Learning denotes added training without a listed type. SFT/RL: supervised fine-tuning/reinforcement learning.

1. Mechanism. D/P/E denotes document/page/element; superscripts T/V/TV denote text/visual/both. The left side of → is the evidence representation returned by retrieval or selection; the right side is the generation input. Without an arrow, retrieval and generation use the same granularity and modality; retrieval-only methods are labeled by their returned unit. Superscript t denotes additional retrieval, scoring, or page-selection training. Parentheses after model names specify evidence forms; semicolons separate independent paths, and an arrow applies only within its path. Brackets [ ] group multiple evidence items, with commas denoting parallel items.

2. Evaluation. Only dimensions quantitatively reported in the original paper are listed. Ret. evaluates evidence retrieval, usually page-level hits, recall, or ranking; Loc. evaluates within-page element/region localization or coverage, such as IoU or region-overlap recall. Exceptions (a): Ret. is document retrieval for DocMMIR, DocPC, NeuSym-RAG, and Agentic Hybrid (EXTRACTOR), document identification for HiKEY, and additionally document recall for HEAVEN; LILaC evaluates layout-element retrieval, and Doc-Researcher evaluates document/page/layout-element retrieval. G^(2)-Reader Ret. measures semantic coverage of evidence statements; LFRAG includes element-ID matching; HierDoc includes region-ID-set F1; MoDora evaluates evidence-node recall and filtering. ReAlign Loc. measures overlap between attention regions and supervised boxes; RGenCite includes VLM-assessed evidence support; Lang2Act measures the proportion of internal attention falling within gold regions. MMRetHeads evaluates pages and layout regions on MMDocIR; LMS-Retrieval Ret./Loc. measure layout-element recall and region coverage.
